open_points.subject: Direct agent access and personal-data disclosure
open_points.text: “An agent's own access to a service … is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel” contradicts “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value” and “the owner alone reads them.”
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on an agent receiving personal data apply only to kernel responses, or also to the newly permitted direct agent-to-service path?
options: K-14 governs only kernel disclosures; a service may disclose personal data directly under its own policy
Agents must never receive personal data, including through direct service access
Direct access is allowed only to values that are not classified `personal_data`
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as applying only to kernel disclosures, as the changed exclusion says.

set_aside.subject: Manifest observation
set_aside.text: “When that digest no longer matches, invocation is refused” does not say how or when the kernel obtains and refreshes the platform manifest.
set_aside.question: What action or observation makes manifest additions, removals and digest changes visible to the kernel, and what is its observable failure?
options: Read the manifest on every relevant request
Reload it when an installation-managed change is detected
Require an explicit owner reload action
Load it only at process start
set_aside.default_guess: Read and validate the current manifest on every binding proposal, acceptance and invocation.

set_aside.subject: Manifest trust boundary
set_aside.text: “A microservice exists for the kernel only as a platform-manifest record.”
set_aside.question: Who supplies and is authorized to change the manifest, and is its content trusted configuration or untrusted input that the kernel validates?
options: Installation-controlled trusted configuration
Owner-managed data accepted through the kernel
Service-published untrusted data
Repository content trusted after digest verification
set_aside.default_guess: Treat it as installation-controlled configuration and validate its structure before use.

set_aside.subject: Operation binding contents
set_aside.text: “An operation binding gives one manifest operation typed input and output ports” does not identify where method, URL, headers, body construction, response extraction, effect class and idempotency declaration live.
set_aside.question: Which record contains the complete mapping between typed ports and the HTTP request/response that an operation node executes?
options: The pinned manifest operation record
The owner-accepted binding
A separate adapter record
A fixed convention interpreted from both manifest and binding
set_aside.default_guess: Put the complete HTTP mapping and effect metadata in the pinned manifest operation record, with the binding adding typed ports.

set_aside.subject: Run pins
set_aside.text: “A run pins what it uses.”
set_aside.question: Exactly which mutable selections and external records are pinned for a run?
options: Flow version and function implementations only
Flow, implementations and accepted binding versions
All of those plus manifest operation digests and selected service-instance configuration
A fully materialized execution plan including built requests
set_aside.default_guess: Pin the flow version, function activations, binding versions, manifest-operation digests and service-instance identity used by every node.

set_aside.subject: Trial corpus membership
set_aside.text: “Each contract version has a trial corpus” and “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” while cases “are not withdrawn.”
set_aside.question: What makes a trial case active or inactive, or does “active corpus” mean every case ever added to that contract version?
options: Every case is permanently active
Cases have an explicit active flag despite not being withdrawn
The corpus itself has versions and one version is active
set_aside.default_guess: Treat every case ever added to the contract version as permanently active.

set_aside.subject: Captured failed execution oracle
set_aside.text: “A failed real execution can be captured into it, so a repaired slot stays repaired.”
set_aside.question: What expected result or pass condition is recorded when a failed execution is turned into a trial case?
options: The owner or author supplies the expected output
The case passes when the former failure no longer occurs and any contract-valid output is returned
The kernel records an expected output from a later successful retry
Different failure kinds define different generated assertions
set_aside.default_guess: Require the capturing actor to supply a contract-valid expected output.

set_aside.subject: Admission determinism
set_aside.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus.”
set_aside.question: Which sandbox runtime identity, interpreter version, standard-library version and resource-limit interpretation are fixed so that the same implementation and corpus produce the same verdict?
options: Pin an immutable sandbox runtime identity in the contract or installation
Define determinism only within one installation configuration
Re-run in the current runtime and allow verdicts to change after upgrades
set_aside.default_guess: Pin an immutable sandbox runtime identity as part of the admission inputs.

set_aside.subject: Schema identity
set_aside.text: “An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
set_aside.question: What constitutes the same schema: byte-identical declarations, canonical structural equality, a shared schema identifier, or compatibility under a schema language?
options: Equal canonical schema digests
The same immutable schema identifier
Structural equality
Directional compatibility
set_aside.default_guess: Use equality of canonical schema digests.

set_aside.subject: Map execution semantics
set_aside.text: “a map of a node over a collection”
set_aside.question: What are the map's observable ordering, output shape, resource bound and failure behavior when one element fails?
options: Preserve input order and fail the mapped node on the first failed element
Return per-element results and failures
Execute sequentially
Execute with bounded parallelism
set_aside.default_guess: Preserve input order, execute with a declared bound, and fail the mapped node if any element fails.

set_aside.subject: Guard execution semantics
set_aside.text: “a guard on a declared closed value”
set_aside.question: What value is tested, how branches are represented, and what trace/output status is produced for nodes skipped by the guard?
options: Equality against one enumerated value with skipped nodes traced
A branch for every member of a closed enum
Boolean-only guards
A guard condition attached to individual nodes
set_aside.default_guess: Use equality against an enumerated value and record non-selected nodes as skipped.

set_aside.subject: Effect classification authority
set_aside.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.”
set_aside.question: Which actor assigns an operation's effect class, where is it stored, and what evidence prevents an effectful operation from being declared `read`?
options: The service declares it in the manifest and the owner accepts it with the binding
The proposing agent assigns it and the owner accepts it
The owner assigns it independently
The kernel infers it from HTTP method or operation metadata
set_aside.default_guess: Store the service-declared class in the pinned manifest operation and make owner acceptance of the binding accept that class.

set_aside.subject: Effect target
set_aside.text: “the owner's approval of the exact operation, target and input”
set_aside.question: What is the canonical target shown to and approved by the owner?
options: Selected service instance
Resolved URL
Service, instance and resource identifier
The complete built request described in settled question 18
set_aside.default_guess: Use the complete built request, with the target represented by its method and resolved URL.

set_aside.subject: Idempotency key contract
set_aside.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key.”
set_aside.question: Where is idempotency support declared, how is the key transported, and is the same key reused after unreachable sends, unknown outcomes resolved `not_applied`, resumes and fresh approvals?
options: The manifest declares header/body placement and one key is stable per effect attempt
The binding declares placement and a new key is generated for every send
One key is stable per run node regardless of resend
Each approval creates a new attempt and key
set_aside.default_guess: Let the pinned operation record declare transport; keep a key stable for one attempt, but create a new attempt and key after `not_applied` is resolved and freshly approved.

set_aside.subject: Trace immutability across waiting and resume
set_aside.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record” while a node may rest pending and later be “tried again.”
set_aside.question: Does a resumed node mutate its original trace, append another trace record, or create a new execution identity, and how is the final node result derived?
options: Append immutable attempt records under one node execution
Create a new node-execution record for every attempt
Keep one mutable node trace until the node finishes
set_aside.default_guess: Append immutable attempt records and derive the node's current status from their sequence.

set_aside.subject: Run completion with independent branches
set_aside.text: “A failed node stops only its dependants” and a run “ends `succeeded`, `failed`, `refused` or `cancelled`.”
set_aside.question: When one branch fails, do independent branches continue, and when and with what outputs does the run become `failed`?
options: Independent branches finish; the run then fails with any successful independent outputs retained
The entire run stops on the first failure
Independent branches continue but failed runs expose no flow outputs
set_aside.default_guess: Allow independent branches to finish, then mark the run failed and retain their trace outputs.

set_aside.subject: Business facts versus retained edge values
set_aside.text: “It stores no business fact” conflicts with storing “bounded values that edges carry” and keeping “Values and the records that name them … for as long as the kernel keeps its traces.”
set_aside.question: May retained edge values contain invoices, analyses or other business facts, and if so what does “stores no business fact” exclude?
options: Business data may be retained only as execution values, not as an authoritative domain store
Only digests may be retained for business-valued edges
All non-file edge values are retained regardless of business meaning
Business-valued traces must be deleted when the run ends
set_aside.default_guess: Allow business data as incidental immutable execution values while forbidding an authoritative/queryable business-domain store.

set_aside.subject: Bounded values
set_aside.text: “bounded values that edges carry” and “Traces carry no secret and no unbounded payload.”
set_aside.question: Where are value and trace payload limits declared, what units do they use, and what observable failure occurs when a limit is exceeded?
options: Installation-wide limits
Per-contract port/resource bounds
Schema-level size constraints
A combination with the lowest applicable limit winning
set_aside.default_guess: Use installation-wide maxima refined by per-contract bounds, and fail the producing node with a distinct limit-exceeded reason.

set_aside.subject: Fixed MCP action set
set_aside.text: “The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.” The primary actions also require adding trial cases, capturing failures, releasing failed runs, rolling back slots, proposing bindings, composing/proving flows and refusing effects.
set_aside.question: Which listed MCP operation carries each omitted primary action, or must the fixed surface enumerate additional operations?
options: Treat `author` as covering cases, capture, bindings and flows, and `activate` as covering rollback
Add distinct typed operations for every primary action
Define explicit subcommands under the listed operation names
set_aside.default_guess: Expose distinct typed operations for materially different primary actions and include all of them in the fixed surface declaration.

set_aside.subject: Recent repair context
set_aside.text: “that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”
set_aside.question: What deterministic rule selects “recent” records, and can an agent inspect older relevant failures when the selected window is insufficient?
options: Last N records
Records within a configured time window
All records for the current contract version
A bounded summary plus explicit pagination
set_aside.default_guess: Provide a bounded newest-first page with explicit pagination over all records for the current contract version.

set_aside.subject: Disclosure proof inputs
set_aside.text: “Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`” and “The flow proof refuses an edge that would deliver a value to an input accepting less,” while “a function's output takes the highest class its execution received.”
set_aside.question: Before execution values exist, what class does the proof assign to each function output and edge?
options: Propagate the highest class accepted by any function input
Declare a maximum class on every port and propagate maxima
Defer disclosure checking to runtime
Prove separately for every possible input-class combination
set_aside.default_guess: Declare maximum classes on ports and statically propagate the highest possible input class.

set_aside.subject: Function output class with no received inputs
set_aside.text: “a function's output takes the highest class its execution received.”
set_aside.question: What disclosure class is assigned to output from a zero-input function, or from an execution whose relevant inputs are absent because of a guard?
options: `open`
A class declared on the output port
The contract's declared default class
Such functions are forbidden
set_aside.default_guess: Use `open` for a function execution that received no values.

set_aside.subject: Error-code criterion
set_aside.text: “A refusal carries a distinct code only where some caller acts on the difference; otherwise one refusal with a reason for the trace.”
set_aside.question: Which callers and branches count as acting on a refusal difference, and where is the complete stable refusal-code taxonomy declared?
options: Every primary-action failure has a stable distinct code
Only machine-recoverable failures have distinct codes
The MCP operation contract enumerates codes per action
All refusals share one code and structured reasons are non-stable
set_aside.default_guess: Have each typed MCP operation enumerate stable codes for every failure that permits a different caller response, with a generic refusal code for the remainder.
